lesson_title: 2 Multiplication and Division by a 2-digit Whole Number

overview.what_it_is: This lesson teaches multiplication and division with two-digit numbers. You will estimate, work carefully, and check each answer.

format_facts.label: Main skills
format_facts.value: Multiply and divide whole numbers by two-digit numbers.

format_facts.label: Number range
format_facts.value: A two-digit whole number is from $10$ to $99$.

format_facts.label: Written work
format_facts.value: Show each step in neat place-value columns.

format_facts.label: Answer form
format_facts.value: Write a remainder when division is not exact.

scoring_factors.name: Correct method
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether the steps match the operation.

scoring_factors.name: Place value
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether digits stay in the correct columns.

scoring_factors.name: Accurate arithmetic
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether each product and subtraction is correct.

scoring_factors.name: Complete answer
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether the quotient and remainder are both written.

critical_rules: A tens digit means groups of ten.
Line up ones, tens, hundreds, and thousands.
Check each quotient guess by multiplying.
The remainder must be smaller than the divisor.
Use the question context to name the final answer.

learning_goals: You will multiply using factors and place value.
You will multiply using the column method.
You will divide by cancelling matching ending zeros.
You will estimate each quotient digit before dividing.
You will adjust a quotient guess after checking.
You will write and check division remainders.

core_method.name: Read → Estimate → Set out → Work → Adjust → Check
core_method.summary: Estimate first. Complete the written method. Check using the opposite operation.

steps.detail: Choose multiplication or division from the question.
Round nearby numbers to predict the answer size.
Place digits in their correct value columns.
Complete one small multiplication or division step.
Change a quotient guess when its product fails.
Use the opposite operation to test the result.

techniques.name: Break a tens number into factors
techniques.purpose: Use known facts before adding the place-value zero.
how_to: Ignore the ending zero for one step.
Multiply by the non-zero digit first.
Multiply that result by ten.
Check the answer using an estimate.
techniques.why_it_matters: It shows why the ending zero appears.
techniques.common_error: Adding a zero before finishing the first product.

techniques.name: Use two partial products
techniques.purpose: Show what each multiplier digit contributes.
how_to: Write the multiplier under the first number.
Multiply by the ones digit first.
Multiply by the tens digit next.
Add both partial products carefully.
techniques.why_it_matters: Each row keeps its correct place value.
techniques.common_error: Forgetting the zero in the tens partial product.

techniques.name: Cancel matching ending zeros
techniques.purpose: Make some division questions much easier.
how_to: Check whether both numbers end in zero.
Remove one ending zero from each number.
Divide the smaller numbers.
Check by multiplying the original divisor.
techniques.why_it_matters: Both numbers were divided by the same ten.
techniques.common_error: Removing a zero from only one number.

techniques.name: Estimate each quotient digit
techniques.purpose: Choose a sensible starting digit in long division.
how_to: Look at the first useful dividend digits.
Use a nearby easier divisor number.
Choose a quotient digit that seems close.
Multiply and compare before keeping it.
techniques.why_it_matters: A quick check prevents a wrong quotient.
techniques.common_error: Keeping the first guess without checking.

techniques.name: Check division with multiplication
techniques.purpose: Prove that the quotient and remainder fit.
how_to: Multiply the divisor by the quotient.
Add the remainder to that product.
Compare the result with the dividend.
Check that the remainder is smaller.
techniques.why_it_matters: The check uses every part of the answer.
techniques.common_error: Forgetting to add the remainder during checking.

worked_examples.title: Multiply by a multiple of ten
worked_examples.decoding: The number $30$ means three groups of ten.
worked_examples.model_answer: First work out $78 \times 3 = 234$. Then use the tens value: $234 \times 10 = 2340$. Therefore, $78 \times 30 = 2340$. The product is $2340$.

annotations.comment: This breaks the multiplier into easy factors.
This uses a known one-digit multiplication.
Each digit moves one place left.
The final sentence names the answer.

worked_examples.title: Multiply using partial products
worked_examples.decoding: The multiplier has four ones and eight tens.
worked_examples.plan: Multiply by $4$, then by $80$, then add.
worked_examples.model_answer: First partial product: $407 \times 4 = 1628$. Second partial product: $407 \times 80 = 32560$. Add the rows: $1628 + 32560 = 34188$. Therefore, $407 \times 84 = 34188$. The product is $34188$.

annotations.comment: This row comes from the ones digit.
This row comes from eight tens.
Adding both parts gives the full product.
The answer matches the question's operation.

worked_examples.title: Divide and write a remainder
worked_examples.decoding: Find how many full groups of $20$ fit.
worked_examples.plan: Estimate the quotient, multiply, then subtract.
worked_examples.model_answer: Estimate $7$ groups. Check: $7 \times 20 = 140$. Subtract: $150 - 140 = 10$. The remainder $10$ is smaller than $20$. Therefore, $150 \div 20 = 7 \text{ r } 10$. The answer is $7$ remainder $10$.

annotations.comment: This checks the estimated quotient.
The subtraction finds what remains.
A valid remainder is smaller than the divisor.
The answer includes the required remainder.

worked_examples.title: Correct an estimate that is too big
worked_examples.decoding: Estimate how many groups of $33$ fit into $285$.
worked_examples.plan: Try a close quotient, then lower it if needed.
worked_examples.model_answer: First try $9$. Check: $9 \times 33 = 297$. This is greater than $285$, so $9$ is too big. Try $8$. Check: $8 \times 33 = 264$. Subtract: $285 - 264 = 21$. The remainder $21$ is smaller than $33$. Therefore, $285 \div 33 = 8 \text{ r } 21$. The answer is $8$ remainder $21$.

annotations.comment: The product is too large.
Lower the quotient by one.
This gives the remaining amount.
The corrected quotient now works.

worked_examples.title: Find litres needed for a journey
worked_examples.input: A car travels $15$ km per litre. How many litres are needed for $240$ km?
worked_examples.decoding: The total distance is shared into groups of $15$ km.
worked_examples.plan: Bar model: one whole bar is $240$ km. Each equal part is $15$ km. Find the number of parts.
worked_examples.model_answer: Use division because each litre covers the same distance. Work out $240 \div 15$. Since $15 \times 10 = 150$ and $15 \times 6 = 90$, then $150 + 90 = 240$. So $15 \times 16 = 240$. Therefore, $240 \div 15 = 16$. The car needs $16$ litres.

annotations.comment: The bar shows the total distance.
Each part represents one litre.
Multiplication checks the division.
The unit makes the answer clear.

worked_examples.title: Pack and sell cookies
worked_examples.input: $840$ cookies are packed in packets of $24$. Each packet sells for $3$. Find the money received.
worked_examples.decoding: First find packet count. Then find total money.
worked_examples.plan: Bar model: one bar shows $840$ cookies. Split it into parts of $24$. Then multiply packet count by $3$.
worked_examples.model_answer: First find the packets: $840 \div 24 = 35$ because $24 \times 35 = 840$. Then find the money: $35 \times 3 = 105$. Therefore, the seller receives $105$.

annotations.comment: Division finds the number of packets.
This checks the packet count.
Multiplication finds the total money.
The final answer uses money units.

common_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting the tens place in multiplication.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The second partial product becomes ten times too small.
common_mistakes.fix: Write a zero before multiplying the tens digit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Removing a zero from only one division number.
common_mistakes.fix: Remove matching zeros from both numbers only.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The checked product may be too large.
common_mistakes.fix: Multiply the guess, compare, and adjust.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The answer no longer matches the dividend.
common_mistakes.fix: Write the quotient and the amount left.

common_mistakes.mistake: Writing a remainder larger than the divisor.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: Another full group can still be made.
common_mistakes.fix: Increase the quotient and subtract again.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using one operation for a two-step problem.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: Only part of the question gets answered.
common_mistakes.fix: Draw a bar model and mark both steps.

time_budget.focus: Recall multiplication facts up to twelve.
Build and add two partial products.
Draw bar models and choose operations.
Check errors and explain each correction.

drills.name: Partial product rows
drills.instructions: Write both rows for six two-digit multipliers.

drills.name: Zero cancelling check
drills.instructions: Decide when matching ending zeros may be removed.

drills.name: Quotient estimate cards
drills.instructions: Choose the best first digit before dividing.

drills.name: Remainder check
drills.instructions: Test ten answers using multiplication and addition.

drills.name: Bar model stories
drills.instructions: Draw bars for four two-step word problems.

practice_plan.routine: Estimate first. Show every step. Check with the opposite operation. Correct one mistake before starting the next question.

mastery_checklist: I can multiply by a multiple of ten.
I can build two correct partial products.
I can line up place-value columns.
I can cancel matching ending zeros.
I can estimate a quotient digit.
I can lower a guess that is too big.
I can write a correct remainder.
I can check division using multiplication and addition.
strategy_notes: Estimate before written work to catch large errors.
Cover later digits while choosing each quotient digit.
Say the place value of each multiplier digit.
Circle the remainder before writing the final answer.
Use bar models before solving word problems.
Check the final unit, such as litres or dollars.
